reconcile.connective: Classical commentators distinguish Isaac as Abraham's sole legitimate son by covenant wife Sarah, so the 'only son' designation in Genesis 22:2 remains accurate even though Ishmael and the sons of Keturah also exist.

discrepancy.connective: C. Dennis McKinsey (Encyclopedia of Biblical Errancy) presses the plain count: Abraham had multiple sons by Hagar and Keturah, and Genesis 22:2's 'your only son' is therefore a factual inaccuracy that no status distinction between wives adequately removes.

skeptic.name: C. Dennis McKinsey
skeptic.attribution: C. Dennis McKinsey (d. 2019), The Encyclopedia of Biblical Errancy (Prometheus Books, 1995)

excerpts.author: John Gill
excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: for, though Ishmael was his son, he was a son by his maid, by his concubine, and not by his wife; Isaac was his only legitimate son, his only son by his lawful wife Sarah; the only son of the promise, his only son, in whom his seed was to be called
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill directly addresses why 'thine only son' is not contradicted by Ishmael's existence: the phrase singles out Isaac as the legitimate, covenantal heir by Sarah — the only category that counts in the divine designation.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley addresses the 'only son' designation for Isaac in the context of Abraham's other sons, defending the harmonizing distinction between legitimate covenant-heir and sons by concubines.
